answer: A harbor admits agents only through dry-dock inspection: each identity anchors one claim to a distinct job completed last epoch, its anchor a signed receipt naming client, task, and outcome, published before payout. Inspectors sample docked claims; a hollow claim with no real job behind it is sunk and its bond burned. Two identities anchoring the same job are both sunk, so a fleet cannot photocopy one job across n clones: it must do n genuinely distinct jobs, paying n real costs, while one honest agent anchors one real job and sails through.
